tool_input.command:
cat >> db/schema.ts <<'EOF'

export const postRevisions = sqliteTable('post_revisions', {
  id: integer('id').primaryKey({ autoIncrement: true }),
  postId: integer('post_id')
    .notNull()
    .references(() => posts.id),
  title: text('title').notNull(),
  excerpt: text('excerpt').notNull(),
  body: text('body').notNull(),
  createdAt: text('created_at').notNull().$defaultFn(() => new Date().toISOString()),
})
EOF
bun run db:make 2>&1 | tail -5; git status --short; cat app/Models/User.ts | head -20; cat app/Http/Resources/PostResource.ts

result:
Post revisions are in, and `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass. I didn't add tests or run the app, so the new routes, the 403/404/redirect behaviour and the revision rows haven't been exercised.

- **Storage:** `db/schema.ts` has a new `postRevisions` table (`post_revisions`) with the columns you specified, plus its generated migration in `db/migrations/`. The new `app/Models/PostRevision.ts` model sits on top of it.
- **Keeping versions:** `PostController` in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts` saves the post's current title, excerpt and body as a revision just before an edit or a restore applies. Creating a post keeps nothing, and a refused edit keeps nothing because the save is skipped.
- **Revisions page:** `GET /posts/:id/revisions` renders a new `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx` with `revisions: [{ id, title, createdAt }]`, newest first, plus a Restore button on each row.
- **Restore:** `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` puts the revision's fields back on the post and redirects to `/posts/:id`. A revision from a different post answers 404, even when the same author owns both.
- **Access:** both routes sit in the existing auth group, so guests go to `/login`. They use the existing `update` policy, so any signed-in user who isn't the author gets 403.
- **Delete:** `destroy` removes the post's revisions before deleting the post; other posts' revisions are untouched.
- **Other files:** `routes/web.ts` has the two new routes and `PostValidator.ts` a revision-params schema. `Show.tsx` has a "History" link for the author, and the `.guren` generated files were regenerated with codegen.

One thing to know: the revision insert and the post update are two separate writes, not one transaction.
